newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan signs new trade accord with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Jordan signs new trade accord with Israel.

text.p: Jordan and Israel signed on Wednesday an amended trade accord that lifts barriers to Jordanian goods to both the Israeli and West Bank markets, officials said.

The accord, signed at the end of talks between Minister of Industry and Trade Ali Abu Al-Ragheb and his Israeli counterpart Natan Sharansky on Israel's Dead Sea shore, extends customs exemptions for most Jordanian goods entering into the Israeli market.
It also removes obstacles to its industry's access to the much coveted Palestinian markets.

"We have gained substantial customs discounts on Jordanian goods entering into Israel as a result of which most of the Jordanian goods will now enter Israel exempted from customs," Abu Al-Ragheb told state televesion.

Abu Al-Ragheb said Jordan also secured a breathrough in eased transport of its goods by a new "door-to-door" delivery of Jordanian goods to Israel. It will apply a similiar method for Palestinian imports of cement and oil and petroleum products refined in Jordan.
Sharansky told Jordan television the accord will boost so far minimal goods exchanges since an October 1995 trade accord, with Jordanian businessmen "now having to pay less in taxes".
He said that "this step is in the right direction, not the last that one, we will make constantly steps to allow Jordanian businessmen to enjoy the fruits of peace."
Officials say the accord has the blessing of Israeli Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu as a gesture to improve ties.
Exports now have to go through a costly and cumbersome "back-to back" system -- taking goods off Jordanian trucks on one side of the border and loading them on Israeli trucks on the other.

Jordanians say the system, which Israel says is dictated by security needs, is protectionism in disguise to keep Jordanian goods uncompetitive in the Israeli market and keep a $2 billion Palestinian market captive for Israel.
Jordan's Transport Minister Nasser al-Lawzi said the new trucking accord will raise exports to Israel and Palestinian areas.

Jordan, wary of the vastly larger Israeli economy, has pressed for wider customs exemption for its products, on the grounds that a three-tier preferential treatment system granted under last year's trade accord with Israel was not sufficient.
Israeli exports to Jordan have exceeded 3 million dinars ($4.2 million) this year against 2.5 million dinars of Jordanian exports to Israel, official statistics show.
